title: Dynamo v1.6.0-glm-5.3-flash-dev.1
text:
Release Notes
Dynamo v1.6.0-glm-5.3-flash-dev.1 is an experimental snapshot build with early GLM-5.3-Flash support on the Dynamo SGLang backend. It is not recommended for production and is not a QA-gated release. APIs, behavior, and defaults may change before stable support. Use it for evaluation, testing, and early feedback only.
Summary
Dynamo v1.6.0-glm-5.3-flash-dev.1 serves RadixArk/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 on Dynamo SGLang. The container is built from lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130-runtime (CUDA 13) and applies GLM-5.3-Flash backports for prefill/decode accounting, linear-attention cache handling, SM100 PTX KDA, and Mamba slot cleanup, plus a scoped cuDNN workaround in the vision encoder. Transformers 5.19.0 and tokenizers 0.23.2 are pinned so image and video requests load Glm5NextProcessor instead of falling back to text-only tokenization (#15751).
Kubernetes recipes cover a 4-GPU aggregated profile on B200 or GB200 and a 12-GPU GB200 disaggregated profile (two TP4/EP4 prefill workers and one TP4 decode worker). Aggregated serving uses round-robin routing and accepts text, images, and video. Disaggregated serving uses KV-aware routing with worker KV events and Mooncake transfer over NVLink, and accepts text and images. All three profiles use NVFP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, EAGLE speculative decoding with ReplaySSM, and HiCache. A shared model-cache download pins revision f46cf340d35a22d0d83d0c1dac8957cf2b1bcd35, and an AIPerf text-trace reference ships with the recipes (#15752, #16387).

About GLM-5.3-Flash
GLM-5.3-Flash is a Z.AI mixture-of-experts model (320B total parameters, 18B active) with hybrid sparse and linear attention and Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections. This preview serves the NVFP4 checkpoint RadixArk/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 through Dynamo's SGLang backend, aggregated on B200 or GB200 or disaggregated on GB200.
Full Changelog
SGLang Backend
GLM-5.3-Flash runtime: Builds the CUDA SGLang image on lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130-runtime and applies upstream backports for prefill/decode latency and retraction accounting, linear-attention hooks and cache accounting, PTX KDA safety and SM100 support, and Mamba slot cleanup before decode preallocation. A local patch disables cuDNN only around the GLM vision downsample convolution. Transformers 5.19.0 and tokenizers 0.23.2 are pinned so AutoProcessor registers Glm5NextProcessor for image and video inputs (#15751).
Recipes
GLM-5.3-Flash SGLang recipes: Added recipes/glm-5.3-flash/sglang — shared model-cache PVC and pinned Hugging Face download, B200 aggregated (agg-b200-agentic, 1x TP4), GB200 aggregated (agg-gb200-agentic, 1x TP4), and GB200 disaggregated (disagg-gb200-agentic, 2 prefill TP4/EP4 + 1 decode TP4, Mooncake over NVLink) profiles, real EAGLE verification by default, and an AIPerf text-trace reference (recipe folder, README, #15752, #16387).
Getting Started
Deployment is Kubernetes-based (Dynamo Platform and DynamoGraphDeployment). GB200 profiles also create a ComputeDomain and require the NVIDIA DRA driver. Full steps — namespace, hf-token-secret, model-cache PVC, pinned Hugging Face download, Kustomize render, DGD apply, and a /v1/chat/completions smoke test — are in the recipe README. The SGLang checkpoint is RadixArk/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 and is not the checkpoint used by the sibling vLLM recipes. Recipes expect registry credentials for nvcr.io.
Known Issues / Limitations
Experimental snapshot build — not QA-gated; not for production.
The disaggregated GB200 recipe accepts text and images only. Video input is available on the aggregated B200 and GB200 recipes.
Disaggregated GB200 workers must share one NVLink clique and require the ComputeDomain CRD and NVIDIA DRA driver.
Synthetic acceptance replaces real speculative verification and is for performance experiments only.
End-to-end multimodal generation with this rebuilt image has not been validated. The image build checks that the GLM image and video processors load.
Measured performance results are not included. The recipe ships an AIPerf text-trace job only.
